title: Tribals suffered most due to Naxal violence, even denied right to vote: PM
description:
Tribal communities suffered the most due to Naxal violence and were even denied the right to vote in the Maoist-affected areas, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Sunday, accusing previous governments of leaving them to fend for themselves.
Virtually addressing a 'Janjatiya Gaurav Diwas' programme at Gadchiroli in Maharashtra marking the 151st birth anniversary of tribal freedom fighter Birsa Munda, Modi said the previous governments remained silent when Maoists forcibly took away children and abducted young tribal women.
"Naxals denied the tribal communities voting rights but the previous governments remained mute spectators," Modi said.
However, the situation has since changed with the elimination of Maoist violence, and tribal mothers and sisters are now blessing the government as they feel secure, Modi said.
Children whose childhood was affected by violence are now getting opportunities for education and employment, he added.
